description: Pinned scenario set for the native-migration reference harness. `scenarios` are existing checked-in `scenario-instance` files executed through the current TypeScript engine; `compiled` entries materialise checked-in portable templates on pinned matcher sites; `situations` are frozen SituationProgram fixtures (Blender-exported generated geometry, recorded-to-policy authority handover); `thresholdCorpus` derives threshold-near variants from a base entry with the engine's own predicate sampling. Every input is an existing simulated fixture or a fixture derived from one through the current compiler/engine APIs; none of them is a real-world measurement, and none is labelled as historical evidence. Coverage labels name the BASE work-package axes each entry exercises.
referencePath: simforge simulate: readInstance -> loadMap(mapId) -> runSimulation(input, { graph, guards: 'collect' }) -> traceDigest

scenarios.note: The only checked-in scenario-instance with a `when` (ttc <= 4.5 s) trigger; exercises the threshold-crossing boundary the plan names as load-bearing.

coverageGaps.detail: Condition-trigger coverage comes from one checked-in ttc instance plus six compiled templates. A deliberately threshold-near corpus (parameter draws bracketing each trigger threshold) is not yet pinned; it must be produced with the compiler draw index and frozen before port comparison.

No checked-in scenario-instance carries actors tagged `ambient`; ambient traffic is produced by the Studio `studio.ambientTraffic` extension (SUMO provider), not by the portable compiler. A reference for large generated traffic requires a Studio-materialised instance to be pinned into this set.

No checked-in instance uses `route.kind: timedPolyline` (recorded actor motion) or an external policy authority. The engine tests cover the mechanism synthetically; a real recorded episode must be pinned before the handover boundary is qualified.

Generated static geometry enters through packages/compiler situation.ts geometry patches with verified bindings; no checked-in executable patch exists in the OSS tree (Blender workbench output is external).

compiled.description: Portable templates compiled on a pinned map through the current compiler (readTemplate -> matchOnMap/findSite -> materialize) and then simulated. These exist because no checked-in instance covers distance/standstill/signal/reaches condition triggers. The reference run writes the compiled instance beside its signature; a native candidate must consume that exact instance, not re-match sites. Entries with `pinnedInstance` are compile-identity witnesses for checked-in instances. Entries with `ambient` pass that profile (and `ambientSettleSeconds`) to materialize; entries with `runtime` record RunOptions the reference applies (written to runtime.json).

entries.note: Recompiles the checked-in curated instance from its template with the manifest replay key (paramSeed, drawIndex, siteId; the pinned site verdict was "degraded", so a rejected site is accepted here). The compiled inputHash is compared with the pinned manifest. On 2026-09-05 the current compiler and installed map data could not reproduce either instance (ec-08: no site matched; ec-04: signal_unbindable at the pinned site) — retained as a current failure of compile identity across map releases, not as a port result.

Generated background traffic through the compiler `ambient` option (applyAmbientTraffic + settleAmbientTraffic, the same path `simforge batch --ambient city --ambient-settle 20` takes). Scripted ambient reactivity (engine default).

Heavy preset with the reactive ambient runtime (RunOptions.ambientReactivity = reactive, as packages/evaluation catalog runs use). The runtime option is recorded in runtime.json beside the instance; a candidate must apply it.
Moderate preset without a settle prologue: the placed cohort is the t=0 population.

compiled.sitePinning: siteId values were selected as the top accepted matcher site per template on 2026-09-05 against the matcher index of the installed maps (matchOnMap accepted sites; rejected sites are never used). A changed matcher index makes the pinned site unavailable and the entry fails rather than silently re-matching.

situations.note: Frozen SituationProgram whose executable geometry patch is a Blender-workbench export (2064-byte normalized GLB + descriptor + three effect proxies, retained by sha256; .corpus/HDRI/catalog source artifacts referenced by identity). The harness applies the declared observer/target sensor transaction, then runs compareSituation against the declared proxy-removal transaction: base leg = proxy present, intervention leg = proxy absent.

SituationProgram with recorded authority [0,6) over a customTimedRoute (engine-recorded track of a reference actor, see fixture origin) and policy authority [6,20) driven by the declared open-loop target-speed schedule through the ActionHook; a parked lead sits on the retained path. rehearseSituation records the exact handover transition state.

thresholdCorpus.description: Threshold-near variants derived at record time: the base scenario is sampled once with AdvanceOptions.conditions at a grid of thresholds around the authored value; adjacent grid values whose first-true tick differs bracket a crossing and become variant instances (only thresholds crossing no later than the base trigger are admissible). Each variant is written as instance.json and executed like any scenario; its result records the predicted first-true time from the base sampling and the actual trigger_fired time.
thresholdCorpus.selection: Bases were chosen because their when-trigger fires from the predicate (not forced by byLatest) in the reference: bus-accelerates 0.78 s, ego-shifts-left 1.14 s, ego-brakes-on-reveal 1.90 s, merge-at-temporary-taper 3.76 s, cyclist-brakes-for-door 6.14 s. gc3 ttc, oncoming-overtake ttc and lane-shift ego-brakes-for-queue never become true even at 3x their threshold in the reference (trigger_skipped), so they carry no threshold-near information and are not derived.
